description: Zafra Radar tracks sugarcane harvest and pre-harvest burning field by field with NISAR L-band radar, fused with NASA FIRMS fires and Sentinel-2, so it works under clouds and smoke. Demo site: the Emiliano Zapata mill area in Morelos, Mexico, where 99.6% of cane is burned and no public record of burn or cut dates exists. Led by a full-stack developer from Morelos who studied in Zacatepec; the method has already been checked against optical data and a grower-confirmed harvest date.
summary:
Zafra Radar turns NASA-ISRO NISAR radar imagery into a public map of when each sugarcane field was harvested. Live at https://zafraradar.earth

In Morelos, Mexico, cane is burned before cutting and the law gives 48 hours to deliver it to the mill. Public harvest figures are published per mill and per week; there is no open record of when each field was cut. Radar sees through smoke and cloud, and a harvested field shows up as a change in the radar signal.

For the 2025/26 season at the Emiliano Zapata mill, Zafra Radar mapped 6,014 cane fields (9,943 ha) and dated the harvest of 3,976 of them, with a median error of 3.5 days against optical reference windows. Its season curve reaches 50 % on 7 February 2026; the official mill report, which the system never used, reaches it on 14 February. The same code, without retraining, dated fields in Brazil with a median error of 2.5 days.

The app has a public explorer and a weekly report view designed for mill staff.
details:
Live: https://zafraradar.earth

Video (30 s): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tSx4YqA8O_Y

Demo deck: https://github.com/JuanToledo23/zafra-radar-app/blob/main/docs/demo/zafra-radar-demo.pdf

WHAT IT DOES

Zafra Radar is a web app that shows, field by field, when sugarcane was harvested, using NASA-ISRO NISAR radar. The public explorer plays the whole season on a map, compares radar images before and after harvest, and opens any field to see its radar history and detected harvest date. A second view, "Mill operations", gives a weekly report of what was cut and what is still standing. It only uses data available on or before the selected date, so it shows what a mill would really have known that week.

WHY IT MATTERS

More than 5,000 growers supply the Emiliano Zapata mill in Morelos, Mexico, according to local press. Cane is burned before harvest and Mexico's sugarcane law (LDSCA, art. 73) gives 48 hours to deliver burned cane to the mill. During the 2025/26 season, more than 170,000 tonnes in the mill's supply area were affected by accidental burns, according to local press. Public figures are mill-level weekly totals; there is no open record of when each field was cut. Optical satellites are blocked by smoke and cloud. Radar is not.

HOW WE KNOW IT WORKS

- Morelos 2025/26: 6,014 cane fields, 9,943 ha (104 % of the 9,565 ha officially harvested). 3,976 fields dated, covering 72 % of the official area.

- Median date error of 3.5 days against optical reference windows (24 of 26 reference fields within 12 days).

- Against the official weekly reports, which the system never used: half of the season on 7 February (radar) versus 14 February (official); end of season 7 May versus 3 May.

- One grower-reported field: the family recalled harvesting on 26 February 2026; radar dated it 12 February, and optical images place the harvest between 9 and 14 February.

- Brazil, same code without retraining: 2.5 days median error (37 of 40 reference fields), with only about four months of NISAR imagery available.

WHAT WE LEARNED ABOUT FIRE

Weekly fire detections follow weekly harvests (r = 0.71), but individual fires cannot be reliably matched to individual fields: the match rate is barely above chance. We removed a feature that depended on it and documented the finding in the repository.

LIMITS

One season. 72 % of the area dated in Morelos and 29 % in Brazil, where the radar record covers only part of the season. The tool has not been tested with mill staff or growers; its design comes from the cane law, public reports and one grower's account.

HOW IT WAS BUILT

NISAR L-band backscatter (GCOV, HH and HV) is the core input. Harvest detection in the research library uses a machine-learning classifier on NISAR radar features. Python, FastAPI and PostGIS for data and API; React, TypeScript and MapLibre for the map; Docker and Caddy for deployment on a cloud virtual machine. Radar is served as map tiles and fields as vector tiles. English and Spanish interface; works on phones.

PRIOR WORK, DISCLOSED

The harvest-dating method lives in a separate research library written before the event (release v0.1.0, 11 November 2026): https://github.com/JuanToledo23/zafra-radar-research. One library commit on 14 November added the comparison with official reports. The entire web app was built during the event: https://github.com/JuanToledo23/zafra-radar-app

USE OF AI

AI coding assistants were used to write code, tests and documentation under the author's review, and to draft text. The logo is an SVG drawn as code with AI assistance. No AI-generated photos are used in the app. Any AI-generated footage in the 30-second video is marked with a visible watermark. Details are in AI_USAGE.md in the repository.
